draft.title: Human evolution
card: Early hominins such as Australopithecus lived in Africa. They walked upright on two legs but had small brains, about the size of a chimpanzee's.

Walking upright shows in the bones. The pelvis is short and bowl-shaped, the legs are long, and the spine curves in an S-shape. The foramen magnum, where the spinal cord leaves the skull, sits underneath the skull.
Members of the genus Homo show a larger brain than Australopithecus, and over time the brain size increased. Their legs were longer than their arms, and their teeth and jaws became smaller.
Hominins did not change in one straight line. Several species lived at the same time, and bones are used to compare their features.
draft.remember: Upright walking came first in Australopithecus. Larger brains came later in Homo.

a.q: Which pair of features best shows that a fossil hominin walked upright?
opts: A bowl-shaped pelvis and a foramen magnum under the skull
A large brain case and a heavy brow ridge
Long arms and a skull with a flat base
Small teeth and a large, rounded brain case
a.why: A short bowl-shaped pelvis and a foramen magnum under the skull both show an upright body. Brain size and tooth size are about the head and diet, not posture. A brain case does not show how the animal stood.
a.clue: Look for features of the hips and the base of the skull.

b.q: A fossil hominin from Africa has a small brain, close to a chimpanzee's, but its leg and pelvis bones show it walked upright. Which genus is it most likely to belong to?
opts: Australopithecus
Homo
Neither, as it has a small brain
Both, as it walked upright
b.why: Australopithecus walked upright but kept a small brain. Homo had a larger brain, so the small brain rules out Homo. Upright walking alone does not place a fossil in both genera.
b.clue: Which genus had upright walking before a large brain?

a.best: A bowl-shaped pelvis and a foramen magnum under the skull

problems.detail: "Upright walking came first in Australopithecus" suggests bipedalism first appeared in Australopithecus. Earlier hominins such as Ardipithecus, Orrorin and Sahelanthropus show signs of upright walking. The card only says "early hominins such as Australopithecus", so the remember line is more absolute than the card. Reword to something like "Upright walking came before large brains: Australopithecus walked upright with a small brain."

The clue "Look for features of the hips and the base of the skull" names exactly the two features in the right option, and no other option mentions the hips. A student can pick the answer from the clue alone, without knowing the idea.

Bullet 2 lists "the legs are long" as a sign of upright walking, right after describing Australopithecus. Australopithecus had relatively short legs and long arms, and bullet 3 presents legs longer than arms as a Homo feature. A student could wrongly conclude that Australopithecus had long legs.

check.summary: Both answers are correct. The remember line wrongly implies upright walking began with Australopithecus, the clue for (a) gives the answer away, and "legs are long" in the card blurs the contrast between Australopithecus and Homo.

proposal.title: Human evolution
card: Early hominins such as Australopithecus lived in Africa. They walked upright on two legs but had small brains, about the size of a chimpanzee's. Their arms were long compared with their legs.
Walking upright shows in the bones. The pelvis is short and bowl-shaped, and the spine curves in an S-shape. The foramen magnum, where the spinal cord leaves the skull, sits underneath the skull.
Members of the genus Homo had larger brains than Australopithecus, and brain size increased over time. Their legs were longer than their arms, and their teeth and jaws became smaller.
Hominins did not change in one straight line. Several species lived at the same time, and scientists compare their bones to see how their features differ.
proposal.remember: Upright walking came before large brains: Australopithecus walked upright with a small brain, and Homo later had larger ones.

a.q: Which pair of features best shows that a fossil hominin walked upright?
opts: A bowl-shaped pelvis and a foramen magnum under the skull
Long arms and a foramen magnum at the back of the skull
A large brain case and long legs compared with the arms
Small teeth and a large, rounded brain case
a.why: A short, bowl-shaped pelvis and a foramen magnum underneath the skull both show the body was held upright. Long arms do not rule out upright walking, and a foramen magnum at the back of the skull does not show it. A large brain is not needed, since Australopithecus walked upright with a small brain.
a.clue: Which bones carry and balance the body's weight?

Both, as it walked upright
b.why: Australopithecus walked upright but kept a small brain. Homo had a larger brain, so the small brain points away from Homo. Upright walking alone does not place a fossil in both genera.
b.clue: Which genus walked upright before brains grew large?
